page: Amazon Web Services r8gn.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 processors operating at 2.8 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance provisions 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs with a single thread per core, avoiding hardware multithreading contention. It is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Local storage is not included, requiring external Amazon Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent data, while networking throughput is defined by a 50 Gbps baseline interface.

Benchmark testing shows high memory subsystem throughput matching the instance's memory-oriented profile. The configuration achieved a PassMark memory score of 3317.5, placing it in the top 10% of evaluated systems. Large-block uncached memory benchmarks demonstrate 285.68 GB/sec read and 134.17 GB/sec write bandwidth, both within the top 25%. Compute-focused benchmarks show standard performance, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 15846.0 and stress-ng multi-core reaching 27292.17 in the middle 50%. PassMark database operations reached 24245.32 (top 25%), while Redis SET throughput recorded 36.51 million operations per second.

Without dedicated GPU accelerators or local NVMe storage, the r8gn.4xlarge is not suitable for accelerator-dependent workloads such as large language model inference, where text generation on a 70B model measures 2.39 tokens per second. Instead, it provides qualitative efficiency for memory-constrained and network-heavy applications by pairing high memory density per core with a 50 Gbps network pipe. Workload suitability centers on in-memory caches, distributed relational and NoSQL databases, memory-bound data analysis, and large ETL data pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gn.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the ARM64 architecture with 16 dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 cores clocked at 2.8 GHz and 128.0 GB of system memory. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 8.0 GB of memory per core and 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without local disk storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier memory subsystem performance, marked by a PassMark memory score in the top 10% and uncached large-block read speeds reaching 285.68 GB/sec. General CPU metrics, including Geekbench and stress-ng multi-core suites, maintain consistent middle-tier scores, while PassMark database operations register in the top 25%. While unsuited for GPU-driven machine learning inference, the instance offers high memory density and efficient networking per vCPU. It is well matched for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory caches, relational and NoSQL databases, data transformation pipelines, and high-throughput network applications.
